[Scientific American](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/amateur-armed-with-chatgpt-vibe-maths-a-60-year-old-problem/) reports how Liam Price, a 23-year-old with no advanced mathematics training, got GPT-5.4 Pro to prove a 60-year-old Erdős conjecture about primitive sets in a single prompt.

> The raw output of ChatGPT's proof was actually quite poor. So it required an expert to kind of sift through and actually understand what it was trying to say.
>
> — Jared Lichtman, in Scientific American

What the article reports:

- **The prompt was a random draw.** Price did not know the problem's history; he was cycling through Erdős problems on an idle Monday afternoon. His occasional collaborator, Cambridge undergraduate Kevin Barreto, recognized the response as potentially real.
- **The model used a technique from a neighboring field.** [Terence Tao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terence_Tao) says the humans who had tried before "collectively made a slight wrong turn at move one," and the model applied a well-known formula from a neighboring part of math that no one had thought to use on this kind of question.
- **Human experts made the proof readable.** Tao and Stanford mathematician Jared Lichtman have since shortened the raw output to distill the key insight. The solution now sits on erdosproblems.com.
- **Tao and Lichtman see broader uses.** Tao: "We have discovered a new way to think about large numbers and their anatomy." Lichtman says the method confirms an intuition he had in graduate school about this cluster of problems being related. Tao also hedges: "the jury is still out on the long-term significance."

## My Notes

- Tao's framing matters. "Maybe easier than expected" once a mental block was dislodged is a very different achievement than the model out-thinking the field, and the lay-press reflex to collapse the two loses the distinction. It slots into Tao's earlier [research-buddy pattern](/posts/20251002-terence-tao-chatgpt-research-buddy/), where the model's job is less to solve on command than to surface where the human had gotten stuck.
- The prompter-as-author question sharpens here. Credit attribution in this pipeline has at least three discernible links (prompter, recognizer, verifier), and the community will have to develop conventions that describe the chain rather than collapsing it into "Price solved it" or "GPT-5.4 Pro solved it."
- If Tao and Lichtman are right about the technique, the value of this incident is less the single proof and more a transferable move humans can now use on adjacent problems, which is closer to how mathematical progress usually works than the ["AI solves problem"](/posts/20260422-proof-generation-vs-digestion/) headline suggests.
- For mathematicians, the practical lesson lies slightly off to the side. Every long-standing conjecture in the file cabinet is worth a single pass through the frontier model now. Twenty seconds is the entire cost; the upside, once in a while, is a mental block no one had spotted.
